summary: SYSTEMIC, NOT DISCOVER-SPECIFIC, AND IT IS A LAUNCH RISK. Generalising what the admin lane proved: `withAdminCapability` types the handler client `any` and `task-messages` builds its client without a `Database` generic, so `display_name` and `primary_genres` produced ZERO tsc diagnostics while breaking both routes at PostgREST. Applying that lesson to discover's own surface found THREE live schema drifts that make parts of the news feed silently empty, plus the SSRF pattern where three identical instances of one defect class produced zero CodeQL alerts. The rule both waves converge on: a tsc error count is a LOWER BOUND on drift, never an upper bound, and the compiler and the scanner each miss whole classes of defect, so absence of findings is not evidence of safety. discover did NOT build any cross-repo infrastructure. This is a request that the release lane consider the gap in CI structure, with three concrete, cheap options and their costs stated.
working_set: lib/supabase/service-role.ts:11 and :32 — the ROOT of the typing gap. `createServiceRoleClient(): SupabaseClient` and `serviceRoleClient: SupabaseClient` both use the bare `SupabaseClient` from @supabase/supabase-js, with NO `Database` generic. Every charter-surface client that is not the cookie-scoped `createClient()` (which IS generic — see lib/supabase/server.ts:11 `createSupabaseServerClient<Database>`) arrives un-generic through this factory. NOT discover-owned.

app/api/feed/posts/route.ts:46,71,120,184,204,238,261,345,394,428,451,455 — twelve `supabase: any` parameters, i.e. the exact `withAdminCapability` shape. The file also holds 41 bare `any` identifiers in total. It is inside discover's file grant, but retyping a 1000-line handler is a separate task, not a security lane.
lib/news/feed-service.ts:1,41,134,156,171,318,374,486,579,602,644 — ten `supabase: SupabaseClient` annotations, all un-generic, propagating the gap into every candidate query.
lib/search/global-search-service.ts:3,41,42,93,115,200,299,354,378,405,436 — eleven more, plus :33 `type LooseRow = Record<string, any>` and :98 `applyVisibility: (builder: any) => any`.

__tests__/news/news-feed-schema-drift.test.ts (NEW, the working pattern this lane proved out: parse the generated contract, check every `.from().select()` against it, allowlist only verified exceptions, and assert each exception stays annotated)
scripts/ci/check-security-exceptions.mjs (the existing registry-validation pattern; a schema-drift gate would sit beside it)
completed: Swept the full discover charter surface (app/api/{discover,hub,search,feed,news,opportunities}/**, lib/{discover,news,search,opportunities}/**, components/{feed,news,discover,search}/**, hooks/use-global-search.ts) for all three blind-spot classes and reported the results with file:line in the task record.

Blind spot 1, un-generic clients: enumerated every `SupabaseClient` annotation that is not `SupabaseClient<...>` in the charter surface — 25 occurrences across 4 files, all traceable to lib/supabase/service-role.ts:11. This is the shared root cause and it is one file, not 25.

Blind spot 2, handler clients typed `any`: app/api/feed/posts/route.ts has 12 `supabase: any` parameters and 41 bare `any` identifiers — structurally identical to the admin lane's `withAdminCapability`. No `any`-typed client exists in app/api/discover/**, app/api/hub/**, app/api/search/**, app/api/news/**, app/api/opportunities/**, lib/discover/**, lib/news/**, lib/search/** or lib/opportunities/** other than this one file.

Blind spot 3, request-derived outbound destinations: swept every `fetch(` and every `request.nextUrl.origin` / `request.url` / Host-header read in the charter surface. After this wave's fixes, the ONLY remaining `request.nextUrl.origin` anywhere in the surface is app/api/feed/for-you/route.ts:27, and the value is read by nothing. The only other server-side fetches are app/api/feed/rss-news/route.ts:186 and :197, whose destinations are the hardcoded `RSS_SOURCES` constant and a proxy URL derived from it — operator configuration, never request-derived, so not this defect class and not claimed as a vulnerability. Every remaining `fetch(` is client-side with a relative path or `window.location.origin`, which is the browser's own origin.

Used the method rather than the assertion, and it found real defects: a script that parses `lib/database.types.ts` into table -> Row columns and cross-checks every `.from(...).select(...)` in the charter surface. That is what surfaced the three drift items now in HF-DISC-002-NEWSCHEMA-ACTIVE-CHAIN-GAPS, none of which any existing gate reports.

Quantified what the guard does and does not prove. Of the charter surface, 5 tables are queried but entirely absent from the generated contract — feed_post_collaborators (4 call sites), poll_options, user_news_preferences, user_news_subscriptions, videos — so for those, no column check is possible at all and only the migration chain is evidence. Conversely artist_music's four trust columns are selected at app/api/feed/music/route.ts:174 where they DO exist in the active chain, so that select is fine and only the contract is stale. A failure of the guard therefore means 'the contract and the chain disagree', not always 'this select is broken'.

Turned the lesson into a gate rather than a report: __tests__/news/news-feed-schema-drift.test.ts parses the contract and every select in lib/news/** and fails on any undeclared column, with a 7-entry ACCEPTED list. It is fail-closed: a NEW drift is red, and each existing exception must stay annotated in source and the list size is asserted, so the allowlist cannot grow silently.
next_steps: Release/orchestrator: consider ONE of these in the CI structure. They are independent; ordering by cost.

Option A (cheapest, ~1 day, no new dependency): a repo-wide extension of the pattern in __tests__/news/news-feed-schema-drift.test.ts — a test that cross-checks every `.from().select()` against the generated contract and fails on drift, with a reviewed allowlist. It needs no new tooling, runs in the existing vitest tier, and is provably able to catch the class the admin lane and this lane both hit. Cost: the allowlist will be large on day one, because the contract is already stale in several places (see blockers), and each entry needs a reviewed disposition. A staged rollout by directory is the sane shape: lib/news/** is done here, the rest can follow per lane.

Option B (~2-3 days, no new dependency): give `createServiceRoleClient()` in lib/supabase/service-role.ts the `SupabaseClient<Database>` generic, then delete the 25 un-generic `supabase: SupabaseClient` annotations across the four charter files. This converts 25 invisible query sites into checked ones in one root-cause change, and it will surface pre-existing drift as new tsc errors — which is the point, but it means the 1,384-diagnostic baseline moves. It is a database-lane or platform-lane change because lib/supabase/** and lib/database.types.ts are not discover-owned.

Option C (most expensive, do not start without a decision): regenerate `lib/database.types.ts` from a real database so the contract stops being a third opinion that disagrees with the migration chain. Blocked on CP-051 and on a reachable hosted database; discover can do none of it.

Whatever is chosen, record explicitly in the release criteria that a tsc error count is a LOWER BOUND on drift. `HF-RELEASE-SEC-CODEQL` already records the parallel fact for the scanner: there is no refs/heads/main code-scanning baseline, so the Advanced Security check's alert count measures the size of PR #14 rather than newly introduced risk. Two independent verification channels are each blind in a known direction; neither one's silence is evidence.

Consider also a `rg`-based check rather than a test, since the standing check that found all three SSRF instances is `rg -n "new URL\('/api/" app lib` and the standing check that found the drift is a contract cross-check. A CI step that runs the greps and fails on a new match would be cheap and would not depend on anyone's test discipline.
blockers: lib/supabase/service-role.ts, lib/database.types.ts and every types/** file are outside discover ownership, so Option B and Option C cannot be started by this lane. discover reported them rather than editing them.

The generated contract is already demonstrably stale in at least one place where the CODE is right: artist_music's four trust columns exist in the active chain but not in lib/database.types.ts. A guard built purely on the contract would therefore produce false positives on day one, which is why the ACCEPTED list exists and why Option A needs a reviewed disposition pass rather than a straight flip of the switch.

5 tables queried in the charter surface are absent from the contract entirely, so for those the contract cannot be the oracle at all; only the migration chain is. A repo-wide guard needs to state which oracle it uses per table rather than pretending one exists.

No diagnostic count was measured. The full `npm run typecheck` cannot run on this 8GB box with 6 concurrent lanes (CI measures 68m18s and 1,384 pre-existing errors across 197 files), so this lane's contribution to that number is unquantified. Evidence here is grep, a contract parse, and source reading — not an observed diagnostic total.

No hosted or credentialed evidence, and no CodeQL re-analysis. Nothing here is confirmed against a running system, and no code-scanning alert is claimed closed: GitHub Advanced Security has no local engine, a registry disposition is not a dismissal, and a local code fix is not a re-scan.
